title: Tennis Match Scoring Engine
prompt:
Implement a two-player tennis scoring model with `Game`, `TiebreakGame`, `TennisSet`, and `Match`. Store raw point counts and derive displayed scores; do not make display labels mutable state.

`Game.record_point(player)` records a point for one of the configured players. An ordinary game finishes only when a player has at least four points and leads by two. `displayed_score()` returns ordinary scores using `0`, `15`, `30`, and `40`; at three or more points each it returns `deuce`, or `advantage <player>` when one player leads by one.

`TiebreakGame` uses raw numeric display and finishes at seven or more points with a two-point lead. `TennisSet` owns completed games and a current game. A set finishes at at least six games with a two-game lead, except that exactly 6-6 starts a `TiebreakGame`; the tiebreak winner finishes the set at 7-6. `Match(players=('A', 'B'), best_of=3)` owns sets, records points through its current set, and finishes as soon as a player has `best_of // 2 + 1` sets. Accept positive odd best-of values; best-of-three and best-of-five must work.

Expose `complete`, `winner`, and `state()` on each layer as useful. Reject an unknown player with `ValueError`; recording a point after its game, set, or match has completed raises `RuntimeError`. Use only the standard library.

example.input: game = Game(); [game.record_point(player) for player in 'AAABBB']; game.displayed_score()
example.reasoning: Both players have reached three raw points, so the ordinary 40-40 display is deuce.
